title: Breakdowns: Motorways & Other Roads
whatItIs: If you break down, stop in a place of relative safety, warn other traffic and keep well away from your vehicle and moving traffic. Never use a warning triangle on a motorway.
keyFacts: The safest place to stop is one designed for parking. On motorways and high-speed roads, that is a service area.
Hard shoulders give less protection than other places of relative safety: they are close to fast traffic.
Other roads: put a warning triangle at least 45 metres behind, on the same side. Never use one on a motorway.
Can't get out safely? Stay in the vehicle with seat belt and hazard lights on, and call 999 for the police.
Give your location using the numbers on marker posts or driver location signs at the roadside.

visual.caption: Motorway breakdown: Go left, Get safe, Get help (rule 277)

items.title: Go left
items.text: Move to the left lane, then into an emergency area or onto the hard shoulder.

items.title: Stop well to the left
items.text: Wheels turned left, hazard lights on. Ideally just beyond an emergency phone.

items.title: Get safe
items.text: Get out on the side away from traffic. Wait behind the barrier, away from the vehicle.

items.title: Get help
items.text: Use the free emergency phone, facing the traffic, or call a recovery service.

a.label: Motorway
points: Wait behind the safety barrier, away from your lorry

b.label: Other roads
points: Warning triangle at least 45 m behind
Don't stand between your vehicle and oncoming traffic

onTheTest.question: Your lorry breaks down on a motorway and you stop on the hard shoulder. Where should you wait?
options: Behind the safety barrier, away from your lorry
In the cab with the engine running
Beside the lorry to warn traffic
onTheTest.why: Get out on the side away from traffic and wait well away from your vehicle and moving traffic, behind the safety barrier where there is one.

onTheTest.question: Your lorry breaks down on a single carriageway road. Where should you place a warning triangle?
onTheTest.why: Put a warning triangle on the road at least 45 metres (147 feet) behind your vehicle, on the same side of the road.

traps: Don't go back to your vehicle, even if it's raining, cold or dark.
Something fell off your lorry on a motorway? Don't remove it: stop safely and call 999.
Leaving an emergency area: you MUST use the emergency phone and follow the advice first.
